payload.name: Extract purchase events from relative-clause modifiers
payload.description: When a noun phrase is modified by a relative clause expressing a purchase, acquisition, or other dated event (e.g., 'that I bought'), extract that event as its own memory for the modified object, with the relative time resolved against the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an object noun with a relative clause denoting a purchase/acquisition and a relative time expression (e.g., 'the X that I bought the day before yesterday'), create a separate event candidate: subject=buyer, content names the purchased object explicitly, and world_start = resolved purchase date.

When checking existing memories, do not SKIP such a candidate merely because the buyer or noun already appears in memory; verify whether the specific purchase event for that object is already stored, and if not, propose ADD.
Resolve relative time phrases ('yesterday', 'day before yesterday', 'last week') from the message/session timestamp so the stored event carries an absolute date.

solves: The diagnosed cause is mis-parsing a relative-clause purchase modifier ('the X that I bought ...') into the subject's existing memory, dropping the real purchase event. The rule—extract such relative-clause events as separate dated memories and verify coverage before skipping—applies to any future message where an object is described by a purchase/acquisition relative clause with a relative time expression.
